page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD for temporary storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mixture of average and strong single-threaded capabilities alongside weaker multi-threaded scaling. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is rated as average at 2287.49, while multi-core performance drops to the weak tier at 4653.8. Single-threaded gzip compression is a notable highlight, achieving a top-tier throughput of 36.47 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and large-block memory write bandwidth are relatively weak. Passmark CPU, database operations, and Redis SET operations all perform in the average tier.

From a resource density and cost efficiency perspective, the D4ds_v7 offers a balanced hardware profile for workloads requiring moderate compute and memory. The inclusion of a dedicated 236 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local scratch space without requiring external storage attachments, though the lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses should be noted. This server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, light database operations, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
